purpose: Tesamorelin is used to reduce excess belly fat in adults with HIV who have a condition called lipodystrophy, which causes abnormal fat buildup in the stomach area. This fat buildup is often a side effect of HIV medicines. It is not a weight loss drug for general use.
how_it_works: Your body makes a natural hormone called growth hormone-releasing factor, which tells your pituitary gland to release growth hormone. Tesamorelin works like that natural hormone, signaling your body to produce more growth hormone. This extra growth hormone then helps break down and reduce the excess fat stored in your belly area.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include redness, pain, itching, or swelling at the injection site. Some people also experience joint pain, muscle aches, swelling in the hands or feet, numbness or tingling, and stomach discomfort or nausea.
warnings: This medication can raise blood sugar levels, so it is used with caution in people who have diabetes or are at risk for it. It should not be used if you have active cancer, are pregnant, or have certain problems with your pituitary gland. Tell your doctor about all your health conditions and medicines before starting tesamorelin. Do not use it if you are allergic to tesamorelin or mannitol.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 2 mg injected under the skin in the belly area once daily. Your doctor or nurse will show you exactly how to give yourself the injection at home. Always rotate the injection spot slightly each day to avoid skin irritation.
